# Conductor

> Compile-then-execute DAG engine behind visual node editors.

A node is a class whose typed `run` signature is its interface. A graph binds each node's inputs to other nodes' outputs or typed-in values. Compile gives an immutable `CompiledGraph` that reports what is wrong; the engine runs it as a stream of events, once per row wherever a series arrives. The host declares its own types and nodes.

## Quick Start

One node takes a single value, the other a whole series; that is all iteration is.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from conductor import CompiledGraph, DType, From, Graph, GraphNode, NodeDefinition, NodeRegistry, Param, Result, Series, run
from conductor.widgets import Textarea


class Text(DType, str):
    id = "text"
    title = "Text"


class Upper(NodeDefinition):
    id = "upper"
    title = "Upper case"
    description = "Upper-cases one text"
    category = "text"

    def run(self, text: Annotated[Text, Param(title="Text", widget=Textarea())]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Result")]:
        return Text(text.upper())


class Join(NodeDefinition):
    id = "join"
    title = "Join"
    description = "Joins every text of a series"
    category = "text"

    def run(self, texts: Annotated[Series[Text], Param(title="Texts")]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Result")]:
        return Text("+".join(texts))


registry = NodeRegistry()
registry.register(Upper)
registry.register(Join)

graph = Graph(nodes=[
    GraphNode(id="upper", type="upper", version=1),
    GraphNode(id="join", type="join", version=1, bindings={"texts": From("upper.result")}),
])
compiled = CompiledGraph.from_graph(graph, registry)   # upper.text is the graph's one open input
ready = compiled.with_inputs(text=["a", "b", "c"])     # by name; by address, **{"upper.text": ...}
assert ready.is_runnable, ready.problems

ending = await run(ready)          # in a script: run_sync(ready)
ending.state.outputs(ready)        # {"join.result": "A+B+C"}: what the graph returns, by address
results = ending.state.results(ready)   # every node's outputs, by node id
list(results["upper"]["result"])   # ["A", "B", "C"]: ran once per value
results["join"]["result"]          # "A+B+C": Series[Text] received the whole series once
```

## Core Concepts

### The Node Contract

A `NodeDefinition` subclass sets `id`, `title`, `description`, `category` (optional `tags`, `docs`) and defines `run`.

- Input: `Annotated[DType, Param(title=, description=, widget=, show_handle=)]`. Without a widget only an edge fills it; without `Param` its name is its title; a default makes it optional; `show_handle=False` closes it to edges and allows any pydantic type.
- Output: `Annotated[X, Result(title=)]` is one output named `result`; a frozen dataclass of `Result` fields is one output per field; `Mapping[str, Any]` returns the computed outputs by name.
- `Any` is a value routed unread; an `Any` output needs `compute_outputs` to type it.
- `**inputs: Single` takes every connected name as one value; `**inputs: Series` takes each as a whole series.
- `run` returns `SKIPPED` on a branch not taken and `Asks` when a person must answer (`-> ... | Asks`).
- Every call gets a fresh instance. What the run supplies arrives through `FromRun` parameters.
- The class is checked when defined: a missing identity attribute, a bare widget in `Annotated`, a return without `Result`, `async def run`, or an unmarked `run` beside `@version` methods raises.

### Versions and Policies

An undecorated `run` is version 1. Otherwise every version, `run` included, is marked `@version(n)`; the highest is current.

```python
class Greet(NodeDefinition):
    id = "greet"
    title = "Greet"
    description = "Greets a person"
    category = "text"

    @version(1)
    @deprecated(header="Use version 2")
    def run_v1(self, name: Annotated[Text, Param(title="Name", widget=Textarea())]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Greeting")]: ...

    @version(2, policy=Policy(retries=2, delay=0.5, timeout=10, concurrency=4))
    def run(self, first: Annotated[Text, Param(title="First")], last: Annotated[Text, Param(title="Last")]) -> Annotated[Text, Result(title="Greeting")]: ...

    @upgrade(1, 2)
    def _split_name(values: dict) -> dict:
        first, _, last = values.pop("name").partition(" ")
        return {**values, "first": first, "last": last}
```

- `Policy(retries=0, delay=1.0, timeout=None, concurrency=8, retry_on=())`; `concurrency` bounds rows in flight, each in a worker thread.
- `@upgrade(a, b, inputs={old: new}, outputs={old: new})` rewrites bindings saved at `a` for `b = a + 1`, one step per adjacent pair. Renames carry lock and content; a name `b` lacks is a fatal `stale_binding`.
- `registry.upgraded(graph, node_id, to=None)` moves one node to a version and rewrites edges on renamed outputs. Compile never upgrades.
- `@deprecated(header=, description=, alternative=, migration=)` retires a class or one version.
- `register` requires versions from 1 with no holes and an `alternative` that exists.
- `GraphVersion(graph=(GraphNode, ...), interface=Interface(...))` is a version whose body is a graph; compile expands it under the placing node's id (`approve/check`).

### Field Hooks

```python
def compute_inputs(self, declared: tuple[Input, ...], values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[Input, ...]: ...
def compute_outputs(self, declared: tuple[Output, ...], values: Mapping[str, Any], arriving: Mapping[str, type[DType]]) -> tuple[Output, ...]: ...
```

One placement's fields when they depend on typed-in `values` or the `arriving` types. Compile keeps the answer on `compiled.node(node_id).interface`. `Refuses(code, message)` becomes a `Problem` on the node.

### Types

A `DType` is a class on a builtin with its own `id` and `title` (`class Number(DType, float)`); a parameterisation uses the class keyword `parameterises`. It never converts or picks a widget.

- `target.accepts(source)`: may an edge land (default `issubclass`). `as_text` formats; `refuses_whole` refuses whole receipt. `describe()`, `dtype_of(annotation)`.
- `registry.types`: node types plus `registry.add_types(...)`; `registry.accepted_as(T)`: ids `T` lands on.
- `Series[X]`: values of one type on an `Index(id, parent=None)`; never nested. A row is a path, `(i,)` or `(i, j)`.
- `Ref("node.field")` addresses one field. `DTypeRef` holds a declared type in a record.

### Bindings

`Graph(nodes=[...])`; `GraphNode(id=, type=, version=, bindings=, locked=, title=, description=, fields=, display=)`. Each input holds at most one binding; there is no edge record. A node id may not contain `.`.

- `From("a.result", ...)`: over edges. Refs on different indexes into a `Series[X]` input gather; refs on one index are a union, and a row covered twice fails with `row_covered_twice`.
- `Static(...)`: typed in. A list on a scalar input runs the node once per value.
- No binding: the default. `locked` names inputs no caller may fill.
- `dependencies_of(nodes)`: who waits for whom; an empty set is an input node.

### Compilation

`CompiledGraph.from_graph(graph, registry)` is pure and never raises for a fault in the graph: each is a `Problem` (`code`, `message`, `fatal`, `node_id`, `field`, `details`). Definitions loaded at run time go in `registry.extended_with({id: cls})`.

- Graph: `problems`, `is_runnable`, `interface` (open inputs, unread outputs), `graph`, `execution_order`, `decisions`, `expanded(ref)`.
- `compiled.node(node_id)` answers for every node compile met, with a `state`: `ready`, `not_derived` (it has an interface, but a fault in its edges or upstream kept the walk from deriving it) or `unresolved` (unknown type or version, a cycle, a refused id or hook). It is a `CompiledNode` (`state`, `problems`, `graph_node`, `embedded_in`; `interface`, `statics`, `runner`, `version` once resolved; `iterates_on` (an `Index` or `None`), `validate(inputs)`, `fingerprint` once ready), or a `CompiledPlacement` for a node whose version is a graph (`state`, `problems`, `version`, `interface`, `embedded_in`, `iterates_on`). Reading what a state lacks raises `NotResolved` or `NotDerived`, carrying the `Problem` that explains it; an id the graph lacks raises `KeyError`. A painter asks `state` first.
- `compiled.field(ref)` is a `CompiledField`: `problems`, `binding`, and once its node is ready `type`, `index`, `receives` (`Iterate`, `Broadcast`, `Whole`, `Group`, `Gather`), `condition` (`Condition`, `Atom`, `ALWAYS`).

### Rows

A unit is a node on a row; it starts once what it reads exists.

- A series on a scalar input runs the node per row; its outputs are series on that index.
- A list returned on a `Series[X]` output births rows on a child index.
- A `Series[X]` input receives the whole series (per parent row on a child index).
- `SKIPPED` at a row leaves the series sparse; above the rows it skips the node.

### Legs and Asking

One `execute` call is one leg. A node returns `Asks(questions=(Input(...), ...), prompt=None)`, or `Asks()` for its declared outputs; it and its readers wait, and the leg ends `graph_pending` with each waiting unit (per row on rows). The answer is the next leg:

```python
first = [event async for event in execute(compiled)][-1]        # graph_pending
answers = {"approve": {"result": Text("Approved")}}             # on rows: a Series naming its rows
second = [event async for event in execute(compiled, state=first.state, cache=answers)]
```

- `state` is a frozen `RunState` (`StateValue`, `StateSkip`, a fingerprint per node). Nothing done reruns unless the graph changed it; `state.without(node_id)` forces a rerun.
- `cache` records outputs without running (`cached=True`). Answering a done unit or an unproduced row raises `StartRefused`.
- `Annotated[T, FromRun()]` receives `from_run[T]` from `execute(from_run={T: value})`; `Interface.needs` lists them.

### Retries and Timeouts

Retries live on the version's `Policy`, per unit.

- Only `ExternalFailure` retries: raised by the node, or wrapped from a class in `Policy.retry_on` (`external_failed`). Anything else is `NodeExecutionError` (`execution_failed`), run once.
- Attempt `n` waits `delay * 2 ** (n - 1)` and emits `node_retry`.
- `Policy.timeout` bounds one attempt: `NodeTimeoutError`, final; the thread is not interrupted.
- `execute(timeout=60)` ends the leg `graph_timeout`; `execute(cancel=asyncio.Event())` ends it `graph_cancelled`. Use `async with aclosing(execute(compiled)) as events:` so a `break` stops every unit.

### Errors

The classes are exported from `conductor`. A failure carries `ErrorCause(code, message, details, row)` on the exception and on `node_error` / `graph_error`; its `code` is one of a fixed set (see "Problem and error codes").

```
ConductorError
├── CompilationError        graph not runnable
├── Refuses                 hook or type cannot answer
├── StartRefused            cache or state misfit (a ValueError)
├── InputNotOffered         unknown with_inputs name (a TypeError)
├── NotResolved             read off a node compile could not resolve
├── NotDerived              read what the edges decide off a node compile did not derive
└── NodeError               node_id, original, cause
    ├── ExternalFailure         retried
    ├── NodeValidationError
    ├── NodeExecutionError
    └── NodeTimeoutError
```

A failed unit ends the leg. Every ending carries `state`.

### Events

`execute` yields frozen models from `conductor.events`, the union `ExecutionEvent` on `type`. The `graph_*` events are each an `Ending` (union `EndingEvent`). Events carry records, not JSON.

| Event | Carries |
|---|---|
| `node_start`, `node_skipped` | `node_id` |
| `node_progress` | `node_id`, `done`, `total` (`None` until every row exists) |
| `node_complete` | `node_id`, `result`, `cached` |
| `node_retry` | `node_id`, `row`, `attempt`, `retries`, `error`, `delay` |
| `node_error` | `node_id`, `error`, `cause` |
| `graph_complete`, `graph_cancelled` | `state` |
| `graph_pending` | `pending`, `state` |
| `graph_error` | `node_id`, `error`, `cause`, `state` |
| `graph_timeout` | `state`, `elapsed_seconds`, `timeout_seconds` |

### Saving a Graph

Records are `ConductorModel`s (frozen pydantic). `Graph`, `Problem`, `ErrorCause`, `Policy` and `Index` round-trip; descriptions and widgets are write-only. A ref is stored as `"node.field"`.

```python
graph.to_path("approval.yaml")          # .json, .yaml or .yml
graph = Graph.from_path("approval.yaml")
graph = Graph.from_yaml(graph.to_yaml())
```

### The Palette

`NodeDefinition.describe()` is a `NodeDescription` (`id`, `title`, `description`, `category`, `tags`, `docs`, `deprecation`, `current`, `versions` of `VersionDescription`: `inputs`, `outputs`, `policy`, `open`, `deprecation`). `registry.describe()` is a `RegistryDescription` (`nodes`, `types` of `TypeDescription`: `id`, `title`, `accepted_as`). Printed objects show constructor form.

## API Reference

Three public doors: `conductor`, `conductor.widgets` and `conductor.events`. Each lists its names in `__all__`; import from nothing else.

### conductor

- Nodes: `NodeDefinition`, `NodeVersion`, `GraphVersion`, `Policy`, `Deprecation`, `NodeDescription`, `version`, `upgrade`, `deprecated`, `Interface`, `FromRun`, `model_of(inputs)` (the pydantic model a call validates through), `Input`, `Output`, `Param`, `Result`, `Upgrade` (an entry of `NodeDefinition.upgrades`), `VersionDescription` (an entry of `NodeDescription.versions`)
- Returns: `SKIPPED`, `Asks`, `is_skipped`, `is_asking`
- Types: `DType`, `Single`, `Series`, `Index`, `Ref`, `to_wire(value, dtype)`, `from_wire(data, dtype)`
- Registry: `NodeRegistry` (`register`, `in`, `[]`, `len`, iteration, `nodes`, `types`, `accepted_as`, `describe`, `upgraded`, `extended_with`, `runner_for`), `RegistryDescription`, `TypeDescription`
- Graph: `Graph`, `GraphNode`, `FieldContent`, `Binding`, `From`, `Static`, `dependencies_of`, `CompiledGraph`, `CompiledNode`, `CompiledPlacement`, `CompiledField`, `Problem`, `Condition`, `Atom`, `ALWAYS`, `NEVER`, and what an input receives: `Receive` (`Iterate`, `Broadcast`, `Whole`, `Group`, `Gather`)
- Errors: `ConductorError`, `CompilationError`, `Refuses`, `StartRefused`, `InputNotOffered`, `NotResolved`, `NotDerived`, `NodeError`, `ExternalFailure`, `NodeValidationError`, `NodeExecutionError`, `NodeTimeoutError`, `ErrorCause`
- A run's state: `RunState` (`values` holds `StateValue` or `StateSkip` entries, `done_units` holds `DoneUnit`s)
- Records (`Graph`, `GraphNode`, …) also have `to_yaml()`, `from_yaml(text)`, `to_path(path)`, `from_path(path)`, plus pydantic's.

### Running

- `execute(compiled, *, state=None, cache=None, from_run=None, timeout=None, cancel=None)`: one leg, an async generator of events.
- `run(compiled, **kwargs)`: the `EndingEvent`; a pause is an ending. `run_sync` is `run` under `asyncio.run`.
- `compiled.with_inputs(**inputs)`: a copy with inputs filled as `Static`s, by bare name or address; `compiled.graph` is then what ran.
- `state.results(compiled)` by node id; `state.outputs(compiled)` narrowed to `compiled.interface.outputs`, by address.

### Problem and error codes

`Problem.code` and `ErrorCause.code` are strings from two fixed sets, and a host translates by code. The sets themselves are not in a door: `conductor.graph.problem.CODES` (with `CATALOGUE`, each code's message and fatality) and `conductor.errors.CODES` (with `MESSAGES`) are library modules that may move, so read them in a test that pins your translations, not in code that ships.

### conductor.widgets

Frozen models with a `kind`; `AnyWidget` is their union. `title`, `description` and `show_handle` belong to the `Param`. No type has a default widget.

| Widget | Options |
|---|---|
| `TextWidget` | `min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern` |
| `Textarea` | `rows`, `min_length`, `max_length` |
| `TemplateTextarea` | `rows` |
| `CodeEditor` | `language`, `min_length`, `max_length` |
| `Dropdown` | `choices` (`Choice(id, title, element)`) |
| `EntityDropdown` | `entity_kind`, `multiple` |
| `NumberWidget` | `min_val`, `max_val`, `step`, `integer_only` |
| `Range` | `min_val`, `max_val`, `step` |
| `Switch` | none |
| `DatePicker` | `min_date`, `max_date`, `seed` |
| `FileUpload` | `accept`, `max_size_mb`, `multiple` |
| `ListWidget` | `min_items`, `max_items` |
| `Tags` | none |
| `TableInput` | `min_rows`, `min_columns`, `column_types` |
| `SchemaBuilder` | `schema`, `allow_additional`, `field_types` |
| `IfElseBuilder` | `operators` (`OperatorChoice(id, title, category, arity)`) |

### conductor.events

Every event record, `ExecutionEvent` (the union on `type`), `Ending` and `EndingEvent` (the five endings), `PendingUnit`.

## Workspace Packages

`syv-conductor` (`conductor`), `syv-conductor-nodes` (`conductor_nodes`), `syv-conductor-providers` (`conductor_providers`), released in lockstep; `syv-conductor[all]` installs all three.

### conductor-nodes

Standard nodes on `conductor_nodes.types`: `Text`, `Number`, `Flag`, `Json`, and the base `StdlibNode`. `conductor_nodes.registry(*, categories=None)` builds a registry; `conductor_nodes.register_all(registry, *, categories=None)` adds to one.

| Category | Node ids |
|---|---|
| `text` | `text-uppercase`, `text-lowercase`, `text-trim`, `text-length`, `text-concat`, `text-replace`, `text-contains`, `text-split`, `text-join`, `text-reverse` |
| `math` | `math-add`, `math-subtract`, `math-multiply`, `math-divide`, `math-modulo`, `math-round`, `math-min`, `math-max`, `math-abs` |
| `logic` | `logic-not` |
| `control` | `logic-if-empty`, `logic-if-equals`, `decision` (routes a value on a `Flag`) |
| `json` | `json-parse`, `json-stringify`, `json-get` |
| `regex` | `regex-match`, `regex-replace`, `regex-extract` (past `PatternNode.timeout` fails `pattern_timeout`) |

### conductor-providers

- `conductor_providers.react`: `graph_to_react(graph)` to ReactFlow JSON, `react_to_graph(wire)` back.
- `conductor_providers.mermaid`: `flowchart(compiled)`, a Mermaid flowchart labelling how each edge is received.
- `conductor_providers.fastapi`: `conductor_router(registry, *, prefix, tags, dependencies, from_run, entity_resolver)` mounts `GET /nodes`, `POST /compile`, `POST /execute`, `POST /execute-stream` and `GET /entities/{kind}`. A graph that cannot run, or `StartRefused`, is a 422. The body is `ExecuteRequest` (`graph`, `state`, `cache`); a per-row answer is `{"rows": [...], "values": [...]}`. `sse_frame(event)` serialises one event.

## Project Structure

```
packages/
├── conductor/src/conductor/            node, interface, dtype, series, widgets, errors, model
│   ├── registry/  graph/  execution/  about/
├── conductor-nodes/src/conductor_nodes/
└── conductor-providers/src/conductor_providers/   react/  mermaid/  fastapi/
```

## CLI Reference (this document)

```bash
python -m conductor.about                 # full text
python -m conductor.about sections        # section slugs
python -m conductor.about rows            # one section (prefix or substring)
```

Or `from conductor.about import get_content, list_sections, get_section`.
